extracted.intended_audience: AP Calculus students, AP Calculus teachers, and AP exam readers/graders
extracted.subtask_description: Scoring and solution-quality rubric for AP Calculus AB/BC free-response questions: describes the 0–9 overall scale, decomposition into earnable points, universal scoring rules, and what constitutes a good solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score scale and question decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Each FRQ is graded on a 0–9 scale (most years). Each question is decomposed into typically 5–9 distinct earnable points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical questions allocate individual points to distinct solution behaviors (see setup, method, answer, interpretation, units). Example: a 4-point problem might have 1 point for setting up the integral, 1 for an antiderivative, 1 for the numerical answer, and 1 for interpretation with units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup point
rubrics_metrics.description: A point awarded for correctly translating the problem into mathematics (correct integral, derivative expression, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded when the student formulates the correct mathematical expression or equation even if subsequent computation is incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antiderivative / derivative point
rubrics_metrics.description: A point awarded for correct calculation of the relevant calculus object (antiderivative, derivative, limit work, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method points can be earned even if earlier algebraic errors exist, provided the method shown is correct relative to the student's setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical answer point
rubrics_metrics.description: A point awarded for the correct final numerical value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decimal answers must be correct to 3 decimal places (rounded or truncated) unless rubric specifies otherwise; calculators used must have the command stated if answer is calculator-derived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification / interpretation point
rubrics_metrics.description: A point awarded for explanation of why the answer is correct or what it means in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For interpretation questions, students should write a complete sentence with units and reference to context; justifications should reference appropriate calculus theorems when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units point
rubrics_metrics.description: A point awarded for including correct units in the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label numerical answers with appropriate units to earn this point; units are required especially in interpretation/context questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decimal precision requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Decimal answers must be correct to 3 decimal places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either rounded or truncated to three decimal places is acceptable unless the specific rubric for a question states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic answers need not be simplified
rubrics_metrics.description: Algebraic answers need not be simplified to earn the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students are not penalized for leaving algebraic expressions unsimplified if they are mathematically correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer-only receives answer point only
rubrics_metrics.description: A correct answer with no work shown earns the answer point only (not the setup or method points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bald answers may get the final-answer credit but cannot receive method/setup/justification points unless work is shown that demonstrates those steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error propagation allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrong algebra propagated through correct subsequent work can still earn the method points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a student makes an earlier algebraic mistake but follows a correct method from that point forward, award method/derivative/antiderivative points consistent with the work shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bald answers and partial credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Bald answers (answers with no supporting work) earn no partial credit beyond the answer point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To earn partial credit for intermediate steps, the student must show those steps clearly; simply writing the final value without reasoning prevents earning setup or method points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crossed-out work policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-out work is not graded; clearly marked (uncrossed) work is graded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a student crosses out work, graders do not consider it. Students should cross out clearly anything they do not want graded and leave the intended solution legible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculator-command requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculator results must be specified as such (e.g., 'fnInt(2x, x, 0, 1) = 1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For calculator-active questions, students must state the calculator command used if the answer was obtained via calculator; otherwise graders may not award method/justification credit for unexplained calculator outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring philosophy: maximize partial credit
rubrics_metrics.description: AP Calculus rubrics maximize partial credit: every step has its own point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students who correctly set up a problem but cannot complete computation can still earn the setup point; graders award points for each correct component independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show every step
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should show every step; bald answers don't earn full credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit step-by-step work allows graders to award setup and method points even when final arithmetic is incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proper notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper mathematical notation is required (e.g., write ∫ f(x) dx, use dy/dx appropriately).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ambiguous shorthand; use standard integral, derivative, and limit notation. Notation errors that create ambiguity can reduce credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label answers with units
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Units are a scored component; omitting units can forfeit the units point and may affect interpretation points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify with specific calculus theorems when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, justifications should reference specific calculus theorems (e.g., Intermediate Value Theorem, Fundamental Theorem of Calculus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A correct invocation of an appropriate theorem strengthens justification points (example wording provided in rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete-sentence interpretation with context
rubrics_metrics.description: For interpretation problems, write a complete sentence including units and reference to the real-world context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses that restate results numerically without contextual interpretation may not receive full interpretation/justification credit.
